blocks.text: Goes here. How to find out who buys, in what situation, to make what progress, and what proof they need first. Specifically: the three-tier taxonomy defining the boundary between TAM, ICP, and Persona; qualitative interview protocols (5 customers, 30 minutes each); mining sales call transcripts and community forums; and operationalizing avatars dynamically via LLM context projects rather than static persona templates.

Not here. • How to answer an objection on a landing page -> 07-LPG • Which offer mechanic kills an objection -> 03-OFF • Brand voice rules and verbal identity -> 04-BRD • Content calendar cadence and channel distribution -> 13-ORG

why: A concrete three-tier taxonomy separating TAM, ICP, and Persona, coupled with an operational protocol for synthesizing 5 customer call transcripts into an interactive LLM persona for messaging QA.
topics: [research method, interview technique, segmentation, avatar record structure]

research method / qualitative interview sourcing, call transcript ingestion via LLMs, community mining across LinkedIn and Reddit. interview technique / 5-customer call protocol (30 minutes each), extracting qualitative insights from unstructured audio/transcripts. segmentation / three-tier classification hierarchy (TAM vs. ICP vs. Persona), buying committee role differentiation. avatar record structure / LLM-based interactive persona project, QA alignment testing for content and messaging altitude (101 vs. 301).

The three-tier distinction: TAM as total market demand, ICP as firmographic company fit (size, industry, department decision-maker), and Persona as the individual stakeholder within a buying committee (their daily tasks, career goals, and specific metric vocabulary like CPL/ROAS vs. Quota/Pipeline). Quantitative research minimum: 5 qualitative customer interviews at 30 minutes each to gather raw conversational transcripts. Step-by-step LLM avatar synthesis: feeding unstructured call transcripts, survey data, and CRM firmographics into a dedicated project to test messaging fit, assess content altitude, and run QA checks prior to publishing.

Skip. Persona templates built around demographic fields and stock photos with no functional job or buying context. Fictional mascots or superficial props (e.g., named teddy bears in meetings). Off-topic banter and personal opinions (e.g., eliminating resumes, remote work brackets, or sports anecdotes).

Scope mix. Mixed (the TAM/ICP/Persona taxonomy and interview methodology are baseline standards; building and maintaining interactive LLM prompt environments across multiple committee personas is growth).
